title: feat(security): design and implement the rule engine architecture
problem: There is no rule engine; security analysis has no execution model.
why: A deterministic rule engine is the foundation of all security findings.
scope: Define a Rule trait, metadata, and registry
Run enabled rules over an immutable context with deterministic ordering
Reject findings whose locations are not in the analyzed input
guidance: Rules must never fabricate findings or locations; enforce this in the engine.
acceptance: Engine runs rules deterministically and validates findings
tests: Engine tests, ordering tests, and fabricated-location rejection tests
security: Core integrity requirement: no fabricated evidence.
docs: Document the engine in the security guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(security): add a findings model with evidence
problem: There is no structured finding type.
why: Findings must carry rule id, severity, confidence, location, evidence, and remediation.
context: The rule engine is a separate issue.
scope: Define a Finding struct with evidence and a stable fingerprint
Serialize to JSON deterministically
guidance: Fingerprints must exclude volatile fields like line numbers where appropriate.
acceptance: Findings serialize deterministically and are deduplicated by fingerprint
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(security): add finding suppression with documented reasons
problem: There is no way to accept a known finding without disabling a whole rule.
why: Suppression with reasons keeps analysis usable without hiding problems silently.
context: Findings model is a separate issue.
scope: Support suppressions keyed by fingerprint with a required reason
Count suppressed findings in output; never drop silently
guidance: Require a reason and make suppressions visible in reports.
acceptance: Suppressed findings are counted and auditable
tests: Tests for suppression matching and counting
security: Suppressions must not silently hide findings.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(security): add a security fixture corpus
problem: Security analysis has no reproducible corpus.
why: A corpus of malformed and hostile inputs is required to prove robustness.
context: No analysis crate or fixtures exist.
scope: Add fixtures for malicious XDR, oversized inputs, deep recursion, and malformed RPC responses
Document the intent of each fixture
guidance: Every fixture must state what it is testing and the expected safe behavior.
acceptance: Corpus runs in CI and all cases are handled safely
security: This is the adversarial test suite.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: test(security): add false-positive regression tests
problem: There is no protection against rules flagging benign input.
why: False positives cause teams to disable analysis; negatives are the defense.
context: The rule engine is a separate issue.
scope: Add negative fixtures per rule asserting no finding
Fail the suite on regression
guidance: Document why each negative is benign.
acceptance: Every rule has at least one negative fixture
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: test(security): add false-negative regression tests
problem: There is no protection against rules silently missing known-bad input.
why: Recall regressions are worse than false positives because they hide real problems.
context: The rule engine is a separate issue.
scope: Add must-trigger fixtures per rule derived from the documented rationale
Assert the expected rule fires
acceptance: Every rule has at least one must-trigger fixture
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(security): validate contract metadata for consistency
problem: Contract metadata is inspected but not validated for internal consistency.
why: Inconsistent metadata indicates a malformed or tampered contract artifact.
context: Spec extraction is a separate issue.
scope: Check that spec entries are internally consistent
Report issues with evidence, never as proof of malice
out_of_scope: Proving a contract safe or malicious.
guidance: Report facts and limitations; do not assign intent.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(security): add WASM safety checks
problem: There are no safety checks on contract WASM containers.
why: Structural checks (section count, size, imports) protect the toolkit and inform users.
context: WASM container validation is a separate issue.
scope: Enforce size and structure limits
Report suspicious but not necessarily malicious characteristics with clear caveats
guidance: Never execute the module; structural checks only.
acceptance: Checks run and report facts with limitations
tests: Fixtures per check plus a benign contract
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(security): harden against untrusted RPC responses
problem: RPC responses are parsed leniently without size or schema guarantees.
why: A malicious or compromised endpoint can return hostile responses.
context: The RPC models ignore unknown fields.
scope: Enforce response size limits and reject pathological nesting
Validate required fields and report precise errors
out_of_scope: Trusting signed responses (not a Stellar feature).
acceptance: Oversized and malformed responses are rejected safely
tests: Tests for size, nesting, and missing-field cases
security: Core protection for the network boundary.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(security): add a SARIF rule catalog with stable identifiers
problem: SARIF output requires a stable rule catalog, which does not exist.
why: Stable rule ids are required for code scanning and finding history.
context: SARIF emission is a separate issue.
scope: Assign permanent rule identifiers and metadata
Emit the catalog in SARIF and JSON
acceptance: Catalog is stable and emitted in SARIF
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: test(security): fuzz RPC response parsing
why: Fuzzing finds panics and pathological parsing behavior on hostile responses.
scope: Add a fuzz target over RPC response bytes
Run a bounded smoke fuzz in CI
guidance: No filesystem or network access in targets.
acceptance: Target builds and runs without panics in a bounded run
